Why overpaying makes a massive difference

If you pay £50 extra one month, it's natural to assume you've just brought next month's bill down a little. What actually happens is better. 100% of the extra money goes toward clearing the actual debt, which lenders call the principal.

Because the debt is now smaller, the bank has less to charge interest on next month. Each overpayment makes the next month's interest smaller still. People call that a "snowball effect". You stop paying the bank for the privilege of borrowing, and you start keeping that money for yourself.

Note: Check with your lender first. Some UK personal loans charge a fee if you pay off too much too quickly. Lenders call these "Early Repayment Charges", or ERCs. Many loans do let you overpay up to 10% a year with no fee.
